description: Layer 2 of the D-04 safety gate: an intent-agnostic lexical pre-screen over raw ticket text, independent of the classifier. Terms are curated for what they denote, not for what they correlate with.

measured.note: Recall is 100% on the two intents that can ground and therefore carry real residual risk. feature_request and unclear_request are protected structurally by the grounding conjunction (0/20 and 0/15 answerable from documentation), so layer 2 recall there is not the control that matters. An auto-derived vocabulary scored 90.8% held-out overall but contained generic template artifacts such as 'only', 'call' and 'nobody'; see docs/DECISIONS.md D-27.
measured.revision_note: v1.1 removed 'planned' and 'request'. Measured on the 500 development tickets: 'planned' caught 0 deny-listed tickets while causing 5 false escalations, and 'request' caught 2 (neither groundable) while causing 6. Removing both saves 11 false escalations with NO change to deny-list recall (67/87), and both groundable intents remain at 26/26. A marker that catches nothing is not a control - the same argument that rejected the derived vocabulary in D-27.
